title: Build the Intensive Language Immersion & Conversational Fluency Cohort Kit for Language Schools, by Fri 11 Dec
description:
Modern language academies (teaching English as a second language, French, Spanish, or Swahili) run intensive 6-to-12 week immersion cohorts where daily speaking practice, pronunciation feedback, and cultural exchange are critical. Consumer chat apps lead to fragmented audio files and neglected quiet learners. This operations kit configures Zedu into an interactive language lab for daily immersion.

Work under this goal:
- Design the CEFR-leveled immersion channel structure: language-only immersion channels (#daily-french-salon, #esl-conversation), vocabulary topic channels (#business-idioms), and instructor grammar broadcasts.
- Author the daily 20-minute conversational triad protocol using native Zedu Buzz audio rooms for spontaneous speaking partner drills.
- Standardize the pronunciation audio critique thread protocol utilizing Zedu's 440px thread drawer for teacher voice-note corrections.
- Create the multimedia listening exercise and vocabulary flashcard library architecture inside Zedu File Management with categorized level access.

Done when: A field-ready language school operations guide is delivered with speaking triad session agendas, pronunciation critique thread templates, immersion channel permission rules, and verified zedu.chat features.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Build daily speaking practice on Zedu's voice messages in threads, and keep live Buzz sessions for weekly conversation only
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Zedu supports voice messages (voice-message components in the web app), which suit daily pronunciation practice better than live calls: learners record when they can, use less data, and the teacher replies in the same thread. Approach: one thread per day per CEFR level with a prompt, learners reply by voice note, the teacher gives feedback in-thread, and quiet learners get a gentle DM nudge after two missed days. Buzz is used for a weekly group conversation. Verify recording limits and mobile support in the app before publishing. Done: the daily thread template, 10 sample prompts per level band, the feedback rubric and the weekly rhythm.

Daily voice notes in threads fit pronunciation practice better than weekly live calls and use a feature the app already has.

Voice messages suit daily pronunciation practice better than live calls - less data, learner timing, feedback in-thread. It verifies recording limits before publishing, so the kit will not promise a control the app lacks.
Daily speaking practice needs an asynchronous surface; voice messages fit that better than scheduling more live calls, and the idea ties it to a feature that exists.

Uses a feature the product already ships (thread voice notes) instead of assuming live sessions, and the reasoning is right for the market: less data, time-shifted practice, and a written reply the learner can replay. Keeping Buzz for weekly conversation is the right split.
